items.summary: Italian regulators have fined social media giant Meta €805m (£670; $887m) for accessing Android users' photos without their specific consent. Italy's Data Protection Authority said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app, which suggests images from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts. The regulator gave Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek separate consent, citing the high number affected, ongoing exposure, and Meta's lack of cooperation. This is among the largest fines ever imposed on a tech giant in Italy.
items.title: Italy Fines Meta €805m Over Accessing Users' Photos

items.summary: The U.S. government disrupted the FaceStealer social-engineering campaign, attributed to BlueNoroff, which stole over $400 million in cryptocurrency across 18 months targeting crypto/Web3 workers and open-source developers via deepfakes and ClickFix lures on platforms like Zoom, Teams, Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack, and Discord. ArticWolf researchers identified 677 targets in 58 countries; the FBI noted more than 900 secretly recorded webcam videos of victims.
items.title: US Disrupts North Korean 'FaceStealer' Crypto-Heist Campaign and Freezes Binance Funds

items.summary: A nationwide airline groundstop on a weekend was blamed by officials on an overloaded legacy Time-Division Multiplexing analog system that disrupted TRACON telecommunications, while upgraded internet-protocol systems held up. Officials deny any nefarious cause and insist the outage stems from aging equipment rather than the recently integrated AI system or foreign actors. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy urged Congress for more funding to modernize air traffic control, noting the FAA received $15 billion over 25 years with little result. The agency faces recurring outages, including a 2023 NOTAM failure caused by contractors deleting files.
items.title: The FAA's IT troubles run far deeper than AI speculation

items.summary: Recent cyberattacks—raising Swedish freezers to 131 F (55 C) and threatening Ahold Delhaize with up to €250 million in lost sales or €100 million in Q4 operating profit, alongside a $6.3 billion Binance heist—expose blind spots where boards focus on breach prevention rather than resilience. Penetration tests verify defenses but fail to test whether businesses can survive an incident; Ahold Delhaize contained disruption within two weeks and restored Belgian online shopping in a week.
items.title: Boards Must Assume Cyberattacks Will Breach and Test Business Continuity

items.summary: Stanford researchers released Memorilla, an open-source memory module that converts a document collection into just 16 trainable tokens (a 194M-parameter component) so frozen Qwen3-8B models can access whole stores without reprocessing documents. The encoder and decoder remain frozen while only the memory module trains across three stages in about 19 hours on four H100 GPUs. On FactKG, Memorilla scored 84.33% versus 80.43% for full context using 108x fewer tokens. It achieved an average of 49.68 across eight benchmarks—topping five—but lost ground on PubMedQA (59.00%) and fine-grained tasks, where compression offers little benefit given short abstracts.
items.title: Stanford's Memorilla Compresses Document Collections into 16 Memory Tokens for Frozen LLMs

items.summary: Huawei introduces the Luterra S2, an all-in-one residential energy system pairing a hybrid inverter, modular storage, and AI management. Its first SiC architecture promises efficiency gains; basic config offers 5 kWh at 3 kW, expandable to 336 kWh with up to 60 kW output via three parallel 20 kW units. Passive cooling keeps noise under 29 dB across -25°C to 60°C in an IP66 enclosure. Huawei targets markets beyond the US.
items.title: Huawei Luterra S2 Positioned as Tesla Powerwall Alternative

items.summary: Leticia Gutierrez, a former Air Alliance Houston government relations director and environmental-health advocate, won her upset victory in a Houston-area congressional district. She defeated a better-funded former oil-industry executive whose contributors included petrochemical companies and Elon Musk. Environmental groups hail the win as creating a green Houston contingent alongside Reps. Christian Menefee, Sylvia Garcia and Lizzie Fletcher. Gutierrez's 9th District includes parts of Harris County and the polluted Houston Ship Channel, where studies found elevated cancer rates and toxic dredge material containing arsenic. Advocates hope she will push for pollution controls as Democrats gain congressional control in January.
items.title: Clean-Air Advocate Leticia Gutierrez Wins Houston's Oil Capital District in Blue-Wave Upset

items.summary: As Democrats prepare to take control of the House in January, Rep. Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) is positioned to chair the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology. Her top priorities center on restoring science funding damaged under the Trump administration and reasserting congressional oversight. She highlights a $3 billion NSF budget cut rejected by Congress, allegations that up to 30 percent of funds may be diverted into slush pots, and severe damage at the EPA—where 20 percent of its workforce has left. Lofgren also addresses declining university research support, noting PhD applications are down about 20 percent and foreign students have dropped roughly 70 percent. She stresses preserving climate data amid concerns that the U.S. is surpassing 1.5 degrees Celsius.
items.title: Incoming House Science Committee Chair Zoe Lofgren Prioritizes Restoring Federal Science Funding and Oversight

items.summary: Tracey Elliott, a Director at Eden Sustainable Power and Co-Chair of the Solar Energy UK Skills Working Party, argues that diverse teams are vital to solar's success. She cites McKinsey research showing gender-diverse executive teams were 39% more likely to outperform financially, while noting women hold only 32% of renewable energy jobs. The UK government aims for at least 45 GW of solar capacity and around 400,000 additional clean energy jobs by 2030—roles she warns cannot be filled from a narrow talent pool. She highlights that women make up just 11% of engineering apprenticeship starts and only 14% of electrical engineering degree entrants, underscoring the pipeline challenge.
items.title: Why Tracey Elliott Says Diverse Teams Are Essential for Solar's Future

items.summary: Abu Dhabi's Masdar has completed its $950 million Lockhart Solar and Storage complex in California, developed by Terra-Gen (jointly owned by Masdar and Igneo Infrastructure Partners). The facility pairs 365 MW of solar photovoltaics with 173.7 MW of battery storage, enough to power roughly 350,000 homes annually.
items.title: Masdar Completes $950 Million California Solar and Battery Storage Project

items.summary: Elon Musk posted on X that chipmaker Nvidia would lose critical deals without ousted CEO Jensen Huang, saying many were 'a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract,' even as he praised Huang's supply chain leadership.
items.title: Musk Warns Nvidia Will Lose Critical Deals Without Jensen Huang

items.summary: Elon Musk warns that several of Nvidia's key business agreements could be lost without former CEO Jensen Huang, whose personal influence over the supply chain and commercial relationships he helped build. Some critical deals relied on a "personal handshake" rather than formal contracts. The departure follows reports of alleged extramarital relationships involving a Chinese businesswoman suspected of intelligence links, prompting an investigation and interim leadership under CFO Colette Kress.
items.title: Musk Warns Nvidia Deals at Risk Without Jensen Huang

items.summary: Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill warns the central bank likely needs to raise interest rates again next month and in early 2027 as inflation climbs toward 5%. He expects wage pressures from a strengthening economy, driven by high energy prices linked to conflict with Iran. Financial markets anticipate UK rates nearing 5% in 2027, which Pill calls not outrageous. However, some policymakers worry rising borrowing costs will strain manufacturing and construction sectors.
items.title: Bank of England's Pill Signals Further Rate Hikes Amid Rising Inflation Concerns

items.summary: The first US AI Music Awards ceremony in Los Angeles on Friday honored creators of songs made partly with artificial intelligence. Winners included Xania Monet, an AI avatar whose Billboard-charting R&B song marked the first by an AI-based act to reach a radio chart; she was created by Telisha "Nikki" Jones. Presenters argued AI music requires genuine artistry and hours of prompting. The event drew criticism amid lawsuits from record labels including Anthropic and OpenAI, who claim copyrighted works were used without license.
items.title: First US AI Music Awards Celebrates Creators Amid Industry Backlash

items.summary: The Cambridge City Foodbank reports donations falling about 10% annually since 2023, with over 260,000 meals provided last year. Chief executive Steve Clay worries the government's October 'Be Ready' campaign may dampen Christmas appeal generosity during a tougher winter season when fuel costs strain household budgets. The bank plans to serve more than 45,000 meals between November and January, supported by match funding up to £15,000.
items.title: Cambridge City Foodbank Faces Annual Donation Decline Amid Government Stockpiling Guidance

items.summary: Microsoft apologised on Saturday for a global service outage lasting more than 24 hours, during which millions of users could not access its apps. Service has been restored across Teams, Outlook, and other products. The incident affected Copilot AI as well, with server issues blamed rather than any cyberattack.
items.title: Microsoft Apologises for Global Outage and Rules Out Cyberattack

items.summary: This episode of a series on the Communist Party of China examines how public institutions should serve the public rather than private interests. It addresses two problems: nepotism in hiring and officials escaping accountability through resignation or retirement. Drawing an analogy to a 2014 U.S. airport case, it highlights nationwide rules restricting relatives from shared government roles, plus measures barring post-office business jobs tied to former duties.
items.title: Public Office: No Favors, and No Shirking Accountability

items.summary: Chilean far-right president José Antonio Kast faces mounting pressure eight months into office, with approval at just 24%. Discontent stems from a fuel-price crisis after his government declined an anti-inflation tool amid rising costs, prompting truckers' highway blockades and protests. Regional parallels emerge: Argentina's Javier Milei (60% disapproval) and Peru's Keiko Fujimori (53%) also face backlash over inflation.
items.title: Fuel Crisis and Protests Pressure Chile's Far-Right President Kast

items.summary: Nigeria's foreign ministry has warned citizens, especially those with health conditions, against transiting through Ethiopia's capital due to its high altitude of 2,334m (7,657ft). The ministry reports that 16 Nigerians with underlying health problems died this year while passing through Addis Ababa. It urges people with cardiovascular and respiratory conditions to exercise caution and seek medical guidance before traveling.
items.title: Nigeria Cautions Against Travel via Addis Ababa Due to Altitude

items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham, speaking at the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday (s8), said the UK has lost more than it gained over the last 10 years and that the Conservatives gave Britain a harsher Brexit than expected. He plans to lead efforts toward a new food and farming deal with the EU next week, which he says could raise GDP by £17bn while respecting Labour's red lines (s9). Burnham remains open to rejoining single market or customs union talks but insists voters remain 'the boss'.
items.title: Andy Burnham says UK 'lost more than we gained' through Brexit

items.summary: In a Nations Championship match on Saturday, Nov 14 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium (Cape Town), Wales ended their 73-year winless streak against New Zealand by defeating the All Blacks 35-28. The victory marked Wales' first triumph over New Zealand since 1953 and broke a 34-match winning run for New Zealand in fixtures between the two teams.
items.title: Wales Defeat New Zealand in Historic Rugby Upset

items.summary: The Dar Hamar Emergency Committee reported that Rapid Support Forces (RSF) killed 10 unarmed civilians across several neighborhoods of Al-Nuhud, the second-largest city in West Kordofan state, since Thursday. The committee described deteriorating security as RSF members on motorcycles attacked residents while looting shops and raiding homes amid a communications blackout that included loss of Starlink service. The report followed army advances near Al-Khuway after intensified fighting across North, West and South Kordofan.
items.title: RSF Kills 10 Civilians in Al-Nuhud

items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says the US raised linking Ukrainian NATO membership to withdrawing from eastern Donbas, calling it a red line for Moscow. Kyiv is not ready to concede territory but would put a comprehensive package to referendum. Zelenskyy dismissed Russia's call for broad European security architecture before ending the war and rejected a local ceasefire in Kostiantynivka as an attempt to occupy the city.
items.title: US floated NATO membership for Ukraine, Zelenskyy says

items.summary: Turkey's President Erdogan and Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim met in Istanbul to co-chair a Supreme Strategic Committee, signing a landmark mutual defence agreement for collective deterrence against external armed attacks. The pact strengthens joint military exercises, defence-industry collaboration and personnel training amid Gulf realignments triggered by the Iran war.
items.title: Qatar and Turkey Sign Mutual Defence Pact Amid Regional Realignment

items.summary: Hungarian authorities uncovered nearly $20m (£14.8m) in cash hidden across the country during an investigation into Miklós Seszták, a former minister under Viktor Orbán accused of accepting bribes through the state transport company; he denies wrongdoing. The National Asset Recovery and Protection Office found wads of banknotes totaling 5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350, and $1,257,100 in safes, forests, and buildings, depositing the sum into the State Treasury. New PM Péter Magyar framed it as ending corruption under Orbán's rule.
items.title: Hungary Unveils $20m in Cash During Probe of Former Minister Seszták

items.summary: On Saturday, Ethiopian Defense Forces chief Field Marshal Birhanu Jula accused neighboring Eritrea of directing a fourth round of TPLF attacks across the Amhara and Afar regions, alleging Egypt supplied weapons and logistics to overthrow his government. He claimed federal forces repelled the offensive while attackers fled to Asmara; he also cited 800,000 displaced youths and an unverified coalition with Fano, OLF, Sudan and Egypt. Eritrea and Egypt rejected the claims.
items.title: Ethiopia Accuses Eritrea of Leading Tigray Rebel Offensive With Egyptian Support

items.summary: On World Diabetes Day, South African health leaders urged citizens to take early action against the disease. At an event in Thembisa near Johannesburg, attendees were screened for diabetes, high blood pressure and related illnesses. Type 2 diabetes affects about 10 per cent of adults; in 2024 it caused more than 6 per cent of natural deaths, overtaking HIV/AIDS as South Africa's number one killer. It is estimated that up to two-thirds of those with diabetes remain undiagnosed.
items.title: South African Health Leaders Urge Early Diabetes Detection on World Diabetes Day

items.summary: Darcy Vescio kicked the winning goal in her 100th game, leading Carlton to defeat Hawthorn in their AFLW preliminary final. Separately, Sydney upset Geelong by three points at Kardinia Park, though a serious head injury to ruckman Piper Dunlop marred the contest. In the next round, Geelong will face Melbourne while Sydney take on North Melbourne.
items.title: Vescio Stars as Blues and Swans Reach AFLW Preliminary Finals

items.summary: Japan and the Philippines plan a memorandum of understanding on oil stockpiling cooperation, with Japanese public and private sectors helping build a national reserve system to strengthen energy security. The MOU is set for signing early next week ahead of an Asia Zero Emission Community summit in Manila.
items.title: Japan and Philippines to ink deal on oil reserve cooperation

items.summary: The former headquarters of Italy's PCI, located on Via delle Botteghe Oscure near the site where Aldo Moro was killed by the Red Brigades in 1978, has been converted into the five-star Thompson Rome hotel. Historic features such as an embedded hammer and sickle sculpture are preserved, while the building now offers 69 rooms at around €600 ($670) per night and a restaurant with 900 wine labels.
items.title: The Former Italian Communist Party Headquarters Becomes a Five-Star Hotel in Rome

items.summary: Modern film promotion has shifted from traditional interviews toward viral, entertainment-driven formats born of social media, pushing stars like Penélope Cruz on Hot Ones to perform challenges for fleeting online moments. Critics such as Jesse Hassenger link this trend to Jimmy Fallon-style journalism, while experts Pablo Muñoz and Sunde J. Sastre warn that virality does not guarantee a film's promotion is remembered or effective. Promotional budgets in places like Spain can exceed production costs—Barbie reportedly spent $150 million against a $145 million budget—and stars increasingly use method dressing to stay visible, though the link between creative campaigns and box-office success remains unproven.
items.title: When Selling Movies Becomes the Show: Hollywood's Gimmicky Press Tours and Viral Marketing

items.summary: The White House confirmed that Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will hold the first-ever three-way meeting of US, Russian and Chinese leaders on Thursday at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Discussions are expected to cover nuclear weapons reduction and Iran, but not Ukraine. Zelensky warned the talks could resemble a Yalta-style reshuffling of global influence.
items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Set for First Trilateral Meeting in Shenzhen

items.summary: Elon Musk signed an online petition, hosted on Stand with Jensen, urging Nvidia to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned two days earlier. Over 43,000 people have joined the campaign, which demands transparency, a fair hearing and evidence-based reasoning for his removal. Signers include tech leaders such as Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Y Combinator's Garry Tan. Neither Nvidia nor Huang endorsed it; signers' affiliations are self-reported.
items.title: Elon Musk Signs Petition Seeking Jensen Huang's Reinstatement as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Microsoft fixed a global outage affecting Microsoft 365 and Copilot for over 24 hours, restoring service after blaming an earlier network capacity upgrade. The disruption reached users in 74 countries, forcing some organisations to switch to phone calls and paper records; Indian airlines reported email problems while NHS staff used paper files.
items.title: Microsoft Resolves Global Outage Across 74 Countries

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated that the bulk of issues regarding an India-US trade agreement have been resolved, with remaining concerns lying on Washington's side. He noted changes had come more from America than New Delhi. Negotiations were complicated after a US Supreme Court ruling struck down Trump tariffs in February 2025.
items.title: Jaishankar Says Bulk of India-US Trade Issues Sorted; Final Concerns Remain at American End

items.summary: India's ambassador to the United States, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, rejected comments by the US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF), which described jailed activist Sharjeel Imam as detained for religious freedom advocacy. Delhi Police Special Cell has invoked provisions of the Indian Penal Code and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against him, with charges including rioting, murder, promoting enmity, unlawful activities and alleged terrorist acts. Kwatra argued USCIRF had no standing to comment on constitutional rights of Indian citizens.
items.title: India Rebuts US Religious Freedom Panel Over Sharjeel Imam Detention Post

items.summary: In his latest GREED & Fear report, Jefferies analyst Chris Wood argues that AI-driven investment enthusiasm has peaked and points to India as an emerging-market beneficiary. He cites attractive valuations—Nifty at 18x and Nifty MidCap 100 at 23x forward earnings—a rising private-sector capex cycle with machinery imports doubling from $29 billion in FY21 to $62 billion in FY26, and resilient domestic fund inflows averaging $4.1 billion monthly. Wood warns that renewed US-Iran tensions over the Strait of Hormuz are India's biggest risk, recommending energy stocks as the only practical hedge.
items.title: Jefferies' Chris Wood sees fresh US-Iran tensions as biggest risk to India, sees this sector as the best hedge

items.summary: After a Friday FAA ground stop grounded US flights due to overloaded routers in ageing air traffic control equipment, officials warn the same failure could recur during the November 26-30 holiday period. Airlines plan nearly 85,000 American-led flights and about 29 million passengers, with Nov 29-30 busiest.
items.title: US Air Traffic Control Outage Raises Concerns Ahead of Thanksgiving Travel Surge

items.summary: A credible bomb threat prompted the evacuation of residents near an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois. Authorities discovered a device Friday afternoon at the BioUrja Renewables facility, which produces combustible chemicals along the Illinois River. Bomb technicians rendered it safe Saturday evening, but searches continued as police established a one-mile zone and set up shelters. The FBI joined the probe; no arrests or injuries were reported.
items.title: Bomb Found at BioUrja Ethanol Plant in Peoria Triggers Evacuation and FBI Investigation

items.summary: A decade after Namami Gange launched, a Bloomberg investigation using 10 years of satellite data over nearly 2,000 km and water tests from 12 sites around Kanpur and Varanasi found large stretches remain polluted despite ₹43,060 crore spent. It tracked turbidity, algae and surface temperature, raising questions about whether spending delivered cleaner water. The government countered that satellite data cannot assess the entire ~2,500 km river flowing through five states with varied tributaries and conditions. Officials acknowledged pollution persists in parts of Uttar Pradesh, treatment capacity is inadequate, and stronger enforcement is needed.
items.title: Has ₹43,060 crore cleaned the Ganga in 10 years? Govt counters Bloomberg report on persistent pollution

items.summary: A 17-year-old girl, Prachi Mehta of Bhilwara, Rajasthan, died after an injection administered by medical store operator Ramprasad allegedly worsened her fever. Her family reported severe leg pain and clotting before she was transferred to Udaipur's Geetanjali Hospital where she died on November 12 following a November 11 injection at around 5:30 pm.
items.title: Teen dies after injection at Rajasthan medical store, locals vandalise premises

items.summary: BJP has launched the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra to engage Dalit voters in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is scheduled to attend the release ceremony of Sonia Gandhi's memoir Belonging A Journey of Love in New Delhi on November 16, marking his second meeting with her since TVK allied with Congress.
items.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay Set for Sonia Gandhi Memoir Release in New Delhi

items.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma ordered a detailed investigation into a Friday head-on crash near Kaziranga in Golaghat district that killed 26 people. The Force Traveller, carrying 41 passengers beyond its 27-seat capacity and allegedly tampered with speed-limiting device (set to 80 kmph versus the stretch's 40 kmph limit), collided with a truck around 3pm; Sarma estimated speeds above 120 kmph from dashcam footage. The driver, age 64, was reportedly a repeat offender whose brakes were faulty. Sarma admitted relaxed traffic rules at a Nalbari Cabinet meeting under political pressure and pledged to reinstate strict enforcement against overloading, speeding, drunk driving and helmet/seat-belt violations, while announcing ₹7 lakh compensation per family—combined with the central government's ₹2 lakh—to total ₹9 lakh.
items.title: Assam CM Orders Probe Into Fatal Golaghat Road Crash and Vows Stricter Traffic Rules

items.summary: After two Friday killings—Kuki woman Kimneineng Chongloi at Taphou Kuki village, Kangpokpi, and four Naga civilians ambushed on National Highway 202 near New Heaven, Ukhrul—the Manipur CM Yumnam Khemchand chaired a Saturday security review. Five people died over two days; the meeting ordered continued combing operations and strengthened local posts. The Tangkhul Naga Long demanded withdrawal of central forces within three days, while Kuki Inpi Manipur issued a 72-hour ultimatum to police.
items.title: Manipur CM Chairs Security Review After Killings in Kangpokpi and Ukhrul

items.summary: Dana Mashoian Walrath, an Armenian-American anthropologist and comic artist, presents The Book of Genocides (Harvard University Press, 2026), a graphic non-fiction work examining ten genocides across history and geography. Grounded in fieldwork rather than archival research alone, the book traces recurrent mechanisms enabling mass violence: seizure of land, scientific racism, medical experimentation, and exclusion's conversion into destruction. Walrath argues every genocide rests on an argument of purity, illustrated through dehumanizing rhetoric likening groups to vermin or cockroaches. Using layered visual-verbal techniques characteristic of 'disaster comics,' the work challenges how populations become perceived as threats without reducing history to mere wickedness.
items.title: The Grammar of Genocide: Dana Mashoian Walrath's The Book of Genocides as Graphic Non-Fiction

items.summary: Sammaan Capital reported a strong second quarter of fiscal year 2027, with net profit rising over 28% sequentially to Rs 312 crore from Rs 243 crore in the first quarter. Assets under management grew more than 5% QoQ to Rs 59,188 crore as of September, up from Rs 56,239 crore at June's close. The company also noted revenue and expense declines year-on-year, while disbursements jumped 62% sequentially.
items.title: Sammaan Capital Q2 FY27 Results Show Profit and AUM Growth Amid Mixed Operational Metrics

items.summary: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd filed its RHP on November 13 with the Registrar of Companies, SEBI, BSE and NSE. The proposed IPO includes an offer for sale of up to 66.18 crore equity shares by Coal India—about 10% of its stake—and is estimated at around Rs 9,500 crore.
items.title: Mahanadi Coalfields Files RHP for Nearly Rs 9,500 Crore IPO

items.summary: Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Abhishek Banerjee was quizzed for nearly four hours at the Bhawanipur police station on Saturday after an FIR, lodged by Arnabkanti Das on May 27, alleged that his social media post maligning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Gujaratis. Appearing under a Calcutta High Court directive, Banerjee vowed to keep calling BJP 'anti-Bengali'.
items.title: TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee Appears Before Bhawanipur Police in Social Media Post Case

items.summary: Director Nitesh Tiwari defends his film Ramayana, which has drawn criticism for depicting warrior Sita (Sai Pallavi). He argues her portrayal as an active combatant reflects older traditions like the Sanskrit Adbhuta Ramayana and Odia Bilanka Ramayana, where she assumes Mahakali's form to slay Sahasra Ravana. Actress Dipika Chikhlia notes uncertainty about such scenes in Valmiki's or Tulsidas' versions.
items.title: Ramayana Director Nitesh Tiwari Defends Warrior Sita Portrayal Amid Backlash

items.summary: Two buses under Punjab's Mukhyamantri Tirth Yatra Scheme collided head-on near Naushehra Pannuan, killing four and injuring around 30. The crash occurred at about 4 pm on National Highway 54 after a Faridkot-bound bus swerved to avoid a motorcycle carrying a woman and boy who attempted to cross the road cut.
items.title: Punjab Pilgrimage Bus Collision in Tarn Taran Kills Four
